newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday for the fourth straight day mainly due to the lively domestic A share markets, traders said.

Securities houses and brokerages continued to borrow large amounts of money, especially in early-maturing contracts, with the A share markets surging and more new A share issues being planned next week, they said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 14.10 percent from 11.50 percent on Thursday.
Turnover fell to 7.88 million lots from 11.50 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Buying in the seven-day contract was very active today with many institutions preparing for new A share issues next week," one tradder said.
Traders said the repo rates are likely to move around the current level early next week.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Friday with trading volume falling sharply, and traders said liquidity was flowing out into the A share market.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market dropped sharply to 1.11 million lots from 5.26 million.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, regarded as a market barometer, closed down at 122.05 yuan from 122.50 yuan.
Traders expect the spot market to have a technical rebound next week after successive falls this week. The 10-year bond is likely to find support at 121.50 yuan, they said.
